title: Convergence Rate of Inscribed Polygon Area: |A_n - πr²| = O(1/n²)

problemStatement.plain: The area of a regular inscribed n-gon converges to πr² at rate O(1/n²). Specifically, 0 ≤ πr² - Aₙ ≤ 2π³r²/(3n²).
whyMatters: Quantifies Archimedes' exhaustion method with explicit error bounds
Classical result connecting geometry and analysis
Demonstrates Taylor remainder techniques in formal proof

proven: cos(x) ≥ 1 - x²/2 for x ≥ 0 (via half-angle identity)
sin(x) ≥ x - x³/6 for x ≥ 0 (via MVT + cos bound)
0 < πr² - inscribedArea(n, r) for n ≥ 3, r > 0
knownResults.goal: Formalize the O(1/n²) convergence rate of inscribed polygon areas

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: 233 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Full proof chain from Taylor bounds to convergence rate. All 7 theorems proved.
builtItems: cos_ge_one_sub_sq_div_two: cos bound via half-angle identity + sin² bound
sin_ge_sub_cube_div_six: Taylor lower bound via MVT on g(x)=sin(x)-x+x³/6
inscribed_area_upper: Aₙ ≤ πr² via sin(x) < x
inscribed_area_error_positive: strict positivity for n ≥ 3, r > 0
insights: Chain of trig bounds: sin²≤x² → cos≥1-x²/2 → sin≥x-x³/6 is the natural proof path
MVT approach for sin≥x-x³/6: set g(x)=sin(x)-x+x³/6, show g'≥0 via cos bound, then g(x)≥g(0)=0
The key algebraic step: n/2·(u-u³/6) = π - 2π³/(3n²) where u=2π/n, via field_simp+ring
Mathlib's Real.sin_lt gives sin(x)<x for x>0 directly
